On the call today, we have with us Mr. Anand Piramal, Chairman; Mr. Jairam Sridharan, MD and CEO; Mr. 
Rupen Jhaveri, Group President; Mr. Yesh Nadkarni, CEO, Wholesale Lending; Mr. Vikash Singhla, CFO; and

I now hand the conference over to Mr. Anand Piramal for his comments. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Anand Piramal: 
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today on this call to discuss Q2 FY27 Results of Piramal 
Finance. I hope you and your families are enjoying the ongoing festive season, and I wish you all happiness and 
prosperity. 
 
An important announcement before we get into Q2 results discussion. I'm delighted to welcome Mr. Dinesh 
Kumar Khara, who joins today as an Independent Director for a 5-year term. Mr. Khara has been one of the 
most respected CEOs in the financial services sector. During his tenure, the market cap of SBI moved from $20 
billion to $90 billion at a CAGR of 47%. 
 
During his career, particularly as Chairman of SBI, he strengthened one of India's most important financial 
institutions and expanded access to formal banking and credit for millions of Indians. His experience, judgment 
and deep understanding of financial services will be invaluable, and we look forward to his counsel and guidance. 
With that, let me now begin with a few observations on the macroeconomic environment and take you through 
our performance during the quarter. 
 
India's financial sector has remained resilient and despite geopolitical upheavals, NBFC Gross NPAs have 
declined significantly over the last few years alongside robust credit growth, particularly among upper layer 
institutions. This resilience reflects the strength of the broader Indian economy. International institutions like 
IMF have revised India's GDP growth projections for FY27 and FY28 upwards, supported by robust 
consumption, capital expenditure and stable forex reserves. 
 
However, rising global inflation will exert pressure on India's cost of capital. H2 FY27 is likely to see a broad-
based increase in borrowing costs in line with the RBI shift from a neutral stance to calibrated tightening. 
Nevertheless, we do not expect any notable slowdown in borrowing activity with liquidity conditions remaining 
adequate. Emerging global risks warrant close monitoring, particularly rising U.S. and Japanese sovereign bond 
yields and the prospect of crude oil prices remaining high for longer, which could amplify inflationary pressures 
and tighten global financial conditions. 
 
Moving on to our company's Q2 performance. Our Growth AUM now stands at 98.5% of total AUM. In Q2, 
Growth AUM increased by a healthy 30% year-on-year. Total AUM grew by 24% year-on-year to INR1,13,112 
crores. Q2 FY27 RoAUM of Growth business was at 2% annualized, 34 bps higher than 1.7% RoAUM in Q2

FY26. 
 
In Q2 FY27, our PAT was up 67% year-on-year to INR545 crores with underlying Growth business PBT of 
INR538 crores. Thus, our H1 FY27 PAT is also up 67% year-on-year and crossed the INR1,000 crores mark. 
Asset quality was stable and healthy across both our retail and wholesale businesses, and we will share more 
details later on this call. 
 
In Q2, we completed a total equity fundraise of INR3,850 crores, including a QIP of INR2,100 crores and 
preferential allotment of warrants of INR1,750 crores to the promoter group. This was our first fund raise as 
Piramal Finance, and we are encouraged to see the response to QIP in terms of demand from investors and 
eventual participation of several marquee domestic and international investors. 
 
In September, we completed 5 years since the merger of DHFL in September 2021. In every possible way, this 
merger has proven to be a transformational one for the company. It provides us a platform on which we could 
steadily build up further. 
 
The acquired product suite of mortgages and real estate lending has expanded to more than 10 key product 
categories, diversified across secured and unsecured retail and mid-market corporate lending. 
 
In 5 years post the merger, our branch network and employee base have further grown by 3x, while AUM have 
grown 5x in 5 years from INR23,000 crores to INR1.1 lakh crores for the Growth business, making us one of the 
fastest-growing retail finance stories in the country. 
 
While a large part of what we recorded on day 1 of the merged balance sheet has naturally run down, the imprint 
of this arguably the most consequential FS mergers in India is visible across our businesses, balance sheet and 
P&L. 
 
In these years, we made gains of more than INR3,000 crores from DHFL's stress book. The large pool of long-
term low-cost fixed rate borrowing rolled over from erstwhile DHFL continues to support our liabilities base. 
There is a tax shield of INR16,000 crores of assessed carry-forward losses, mostly arising from DHFL still 
available to us. 
 
As the youngest NBFC among India's upper layer NBFCs, we are privileged to be serving over 6.5 million 
customers across semi-urban India, combining physical distribution with technology and AI in our processes. 
With a AA+ rating and demonstrated retail-led diversified business model at scale, we are confident in our ability 
to deliver steady and healthy earnings growth. 
 
With that, I'll hand over to Jairam to share more details on the results.

should continue to progress towards our goal of 4.5x to 5x in the medium term. Let's go now into some of the 
components of our return on AUM, starting with margins. 
 
The company's net income margin was flat quarter-on-quarter at 6.5%, which you can see on Slide 50. This is 
very close to the level for our overall Growth book net interest margin at 6.8%. And of course, it will get closer 
still as the legacy book goes off our portfolio. 
 
Cost of borrowing. Of course, a lot of attention has been placed justifiably on the liability side of NBFC books. 
I'd like to draw your attention to Slides 16, 17 and 18 for a discussion on our cost of borrowing. 
 
Our incremental cost of borrowing at Piramal Finance continues to decline steadily. Following our domestic 
rating upgrades to AA+ between January and March 2026, cost of incremental long-term borrowing has declined 
from 9.36% in H1 FY26 to 8.67% in H2 and further to 8.46% in H1 FY27. We have roughly INR37,500 crores 
of long-term borrowings, which are due for maturity in the next 18 months.

first quarter. This small delta is largely driven by the higher number of days in the second quarter versus the first 
quarter. Other income was stable Q-o-Q. If you recall, in Q1, we had made and disclosed a considered strategic 
choice to perform fewer debt assignment transactions, resulting in a reduction in our other income line and an 
increase in ongoing annuity. 
 
Moving on to insurance. Following the 23rd September consultation paper from IRDAI, we had disclosed on 
24th September, our initial assessment of how our insurance commission income is likely to be impacted. The 
company currently exclusively distributes life insurance products of Pramerica Life Insurance, where we have 
50% stake as a promoter. If the consultation paper is implemented as it is with an effective date of 1st April 2027, 
we estimate a gross reduction in insurance commissions, potentially having 18 to 24 basis points of impact on 
FY28 return on assets. However, that is at a gross level. Any improvement in economics of Pramerica Life 
Insurance will flow back proportionately to Piramal Finance during consolidation. Thus, the company has a 
natural hedge and a claw-back available in the way the company is structured. 
 
Apart from this, there are other levers that are available to the company as well. For instance, rationalization of 
sales incentives for selling of insurance and other forms of product claw-backs. We believe this can significantly 
cushion the impact on profitability on a net basis in FY28 and beyond. In the near term, the company remains 
confident of meeting our earlier stated FY27 profit growth guidance of 50% profit growth year-on-year.  
 
Retail opex to AUM declined by 5 basis points on a quarter-on-quarter basis to 3.48%. You will see this on Slide 
22. You will notice that we have now consistently reduced our opex to AUM for almost 4 years. While we are 
now well in the target range of retail opex to AUM, the ratio continues to move downwards. The continued 
productivity gains for our employees and branches, we believe, have the potential to take retail opex to AUM to 
further lower levels over FY27. The reduction in retail opex to AUM has driven Growth business opex to AUM 
down 33 basis points year-on-year to 3.2%. 
 
At a company level, our cost to income was 52% in the second quarter, down from 61% in the second quarter 
last year and 65% in second quarter of FY25, as you will see on Slide 52.  
 
Tech and AI have been key enablers of both our growth and our productivity enhancements. Slides 33 and 34 
show some details of our enterprise AI strategy, which we have called Piramal.ai. On Slide 33, the dashboard 
that we regularly share shows progress of AI use cases across all aspects of our business, such as sales, 
underwriting, collections, audit and compliance, customer experience and people management. Like every 
quarter, this quarter, we have put a spotlight on one area heavily impacted by AI. And this time, on Slide 34, we 
have covered customer experience, CX.ai.

Most impactful use cases of AI in customer experience have been Gen AI-powered automation of routine service 
e-mails, allowing human agents to focus more on cross-sell to these customers, leading to a 5x increase in cross-
sell productivity of human agents versus what it looked like before AI took over e-mail response. 
 
PIA, our self-service AI assistant, interacts with customers across WhatsApp and Piramal app, resulting in 6.3 
lakh interactions in the second quarter for queries, payments and new loan offers. PIA also generated 20% of our 
total cross-sell leads during the quarter. 
 
Our conversational AI powered bots resulted in INR102 crores of PIA's cross-sell in the second quarter and 
INR172 crores of end-to-end collection of overdue EMIs and fees in a human-free manner. You can see how 
CX.ai is boosting our productivity, digital engagement and cross-sell. 
 
Moving to risk. Credit risk across the portfolio continued to see the strength that we witnessed in Q1. All risk 
metrics, both early and late across both secured and unsecured continue to look very strong. Our overall retail 
90-plus delinquency is at 0.7%, stable in a narrow range of 0.6% to 0.8% over the last 4 years. Growth business 
credit cost was down by 10 bps quarter-on-quarter to 1.5%. Unsecured, in particular, shows risk at multiyear 
lows and delinquencies at one-third of peak levels. There are 4 additional dimensions, which I would like to share 
specific risk insights on. 
 
First, in the IT sector, the last quarter, I had mentioned emerging risk challenges in home loans for IT sector 
customers from South India. That situation persists. The good news, however, is that it has not spread to other 
adjacent segments.  
 
The second is on the monsoon impact. The weak monsoon does not seem to have had a negative impact on 
Agri income customers, at least so far. Bounce rate in this customer segment was the same as in the first quarter 
FY27 and 110 basis points lower than the second quarter FY26.  
 
Leverage at the customer level, overall leverage levels continue to be low. We have indeed seen some increase 
in leverage in digital lending business in Q4 and Q1, but that has subsided back down in the second quarter. As 
of this quarter, leverage of customers applying for loans from us is lower than it was 2 years ago in every single 
product category. 
 
The fourth dimension on which I want to add some risk insight is on gold loans. This is an important area of 
emerging risk in our mind, which is the rapidly increasing presence of gold loans on customer files. Two years 
ago, on our portfolio, depending on product, 20% to 25% of customers had an active gold loan outside. That 
number is now above 35% in all product categories. Secondly, in financial year '26, across the industry, 
approximately INR4.7 lakh crores of gold loan disbursements happened to customers in deep delinquency, i.e., 
more than 90 days past due. Today, presence of a gold loan on files is not yet an indicator of higher risk in the 
portfolio. However, we believe that these data points that I just shared are worth noting and tracking. 
 
Lastly, along with growth and profitability, we have been equally focused on predictability and consistency. If 
you look at Slide Number 6, our second quarter PAT of INR545 crores has kept up the steady and predictable 
earnings trajectory of the last 8 to 10 quarters. Our trailing 12-month EPS growth is currently running at 155% 
year-on-year. We disclosed long-term 4-year plus quarterly data across most key parameters, showing the 
discipline and rigor that go into delivering predictability and consistency. Our risk chart, for example, cover both 
vertical and horizontal risk across the portfolio and across individual products for 4-plus years. 
 
With the transformation journey of the last 5 years since DHFL merger behind us, the recently concluded capital

release in our balance sheet, likely over the next 12 to 24 months. That, combined with our recent capital raise
